description:
Built-in type CONSTRUCTORS are represented three inconsistent ways, with gaps. This is type-system completeness; it is NOT a blocker for protocol dispatch (fz-bin), which dispatches on resolved Tys, not source type names -- fix it on its own merits.

GROUNDED (resolve.rs + type_expr.rs):
1. STRUCTURAL TypeExpr variants: [T] List, {T,U} Tuple, %Mod{...} StructRecord, (A,B)->R Arrow, A|B Union, literals.
2. NAMED nullary builtins: Builtin enum + builtin_from_name (asserts no args) -- nil/bool/integer/float/cpointer/binary/atom/any/never/utf8/pid/ref.
3. NAMED parametric builtins: 'list', 'resource' -- INLINE special-cases in classify_name (resolve.rs:332-337), because the Builtin enum is nullary-only.

SYMPTOMS:
- 'list' is expressible THREE ways ([T], 'list', 'list(T)'); redundant.
- 'map' is expressible ZERO ways: no %{K=>V} TypeExpr variant, not a builtin, not special-cased, no alias -> ':: map' = 'unknown type name map'. The type LANGUAGE cannot express a map type at all, despite maps being a first-class value (Map module, map_top, Enumerable Map impl).
- Adding 'if name == "map"' would be a FOURTH ad-hoc patch on the parametric-special-case pattern -- slop.

INTENT / FIX (one source of truth, correct by construction):
- Unify built-in type-constructor resolution: a single registry mapping name -> (arity, constructor) covering BOTH nullary and parametric, retiring the inline 'list'/'resource' special-cases.
- Make maps first-class in the type language: a %{K=>V} structural form (parity with [T] for lists) and/or a uniform map(k,v) constructor.
- Audit the full constructor set (list, map, tuple, resource, scalars) for parity.

VERIFY: ':: map', map(k,v), %{...} type, ':: list', ':: tuple' all resolve; type_expr resolution tests; lib+matrix green. RELATED (sibling foundational gap, also independent): fz-bv3 (Region::Type over a struct type panics at runtime).
title: [BUG] Built-in type constructors resolved 3 inconsistent ways; no map type
